newsitem.title: USA: ComEd Dresden 3 nuke seen on line Friday.
newsitem.headline: ComEd Dresden 3 nuke seen on line Friday.

text.p: Commonwealth Edison Co's (ComEd) 794 megawatt (MW) Dresden nuclear power unit 3 should resume electricity production Friday following a maintenance outage, a company spokesman said.
"We expect it to synch to the (electricity) grid later today," spokesman Gary Wald said Friday.
The unit, located in Morris, Ill., was shut Oct 26 for maintenance.
Dresden 3 would likely ramp up to full power production over the weekend, Wald said.
Separately, ComEd's 1,105 MW Byron nuclear power unit 2 was expected to return to full power over the weekend after cutting output to 20 percent of capacity for repairs, the spokesman said.
"We had to do some work on a feedwater regulation valve, but that work should be done later today, and it should return to (full) load over the weekend," Wald said.
The Byron 2 unit is located in Byron, Ill.
Also, the 1,040 MW Zion nuclear power unit 2 was expected to return to service in early February following a maintenance and refueling outage, Wald said.
Zion 2, located in Zion, Ill., was shut Sept 18 for the maintenance.
Commonwealth Edison is a subsidiary of Unicom Corp.
